title: Traveling waves — OpenStax University Physics
text: A traveling disturbance transfers energy. Mechanical waves need a medium; electromagnetic waves do not. Amplitude is maximum displacement from equilibrium. Wavelength λ is the spatial distance between adjacent equal-phase points; frequency f counts cycles per second (Hz = 1/s), and period T is seconds per cycle. For a periodic traveling wave, v = fλ = λ/T. The units multiply as (1/s) × m = m/s: no seconds are multiplied or cancelled. At constant speed, doubling frequency halves wavelength. Amplitude is not a term in this speed equation. In a linear string model speed depends on tension and linear mass density, not how far the hand moves. Holding string-wave speed fixed requires fixed tension and linear density, not a fixed hand speed. Repeated splashes are broadband pulses, not necessarily a monochromatic 1 Hz wave. Use a periodic wave-maker or vibrating string for a frequency example.

title: Types of waves — OpenStax Physics
text: Water-surface waves combine transverse and longitudinal motion. In the simplified model particles move in approximately circular or elliptical orbits, instead of travelling outward with the crests. A floating object mostly moves locally as the disturbance passes. This describes the basic wave motion, rather than claiming that real oceans and ponds can never have currents or net transport. Avoid calling water-surface waves purely transverse.

title: Exponents — OpenStax Prealgebra
text: For a positive whole-number exponent, a^n uses n copies of a as factors. In particular a² = a × a, whereas doubling is 2a = a + a. A square grid with n rows and n columns has n² cells total, not n² cells per side. Check that the row and column counts in every example match the stated total. A principal square root is nonnegative and reverses squaring of a nonnegative number; √(a²) = |a| for real a.

title: Shifts in demand and supply — OpenStax
text: A change in a good’s own price changes quantity demanded along its demand curve, other things equal. A shift means a different quantity demanded at each given price. Higher income shifts demand right for a normal good, but left for an inferior good. If two goods are substitutes, a rise in the price of one tends to increase demand for the other; complements have the opposite relationship. State these assumptions rather than claiming the goods must be substitutes or normal. Ceteris paribus means analysing one change while holding other relevant factors constant.

title: Organic molecules and photosynthesis — OpenStax Biology
text: Plants use energy captured from light to incorporate carbon from atmospheric carbon dioxide into organic molecules. Their carbon does not mainly come from soil. Distinguish dry organic matter from fresh mass, which includes much water. Photosynthesis stores captured energy in organic molecules; cellular respiration releases usable energy from those molecules. Living plant cells respire both during the day and at night. Photosynthesis requires light-dependent reactions; respiration is not the only metabolic activity at night. A plant’s net gas exchange depends on the balance of photosynthesis and respiration. Carbon atoms in organic molecules originate from CO₂; do not say that every atom or almost all dry biomass comes exclusively from CO₂, because water and mineral nutrients also supply atoms. Net carbon gain over a day is conditional on photosynthesis exceeding respiratory losses, not guaranteed.

title: Structures: rectangular sections — MIT OpenCourseWare
text: For elastic beam bending, flexural rigidity is E × I, where E is Young’s modulus and I is the second moment of cross-sectional area about the relevant bending axis. For a rectangle I = b h³ / 12. Holding width, material and other conditions fixed, doubling depth increases I and elastic bending rigidity eightfold. This is a stiffness relationship, not an eightfold increase in every measure of strength. A second moment of area describes geometry; Young’s modulus describes elastic material response. Stiffness concerns deflection; strength concerns allowable stress, yielding or failure. Simple beam models require appropriate linear elastic and geometric assumptions. For bending stress, σ_max = M c / I = M / S; S = I/c is the elastic section modulus. For a rectangular section S = b h²/6. With fixed material and width, doubling depth raises the elastic bending moment at a given limiting stress fourfold, while flexural rigidity grows eightfold. Cross-sectional area alone does not determine bending strength. The plane-sections assumption does not mean layers slide past one another. In symmetric homogeneous linear elastic pure bending, the neutral axis passes through the centroid; curvature comes from varying longitudinal strain across the depth, not a shift of the neutral axis.

title: 1914 timeline — National Army Museum
text: Chronology of the 1914 crisis: 28 June: Franz Ferdinand assassinated in Sarajevo. 5 July: Germany assures Austria-Hungary of support. 23 July: Austria-Hungary delivers its ultimatum to Serbia. 28 July: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia. 30 July: Russia orders general mobilisation (IWM account). 1 August: Germany declares war on Russia. 3 August: Germany declares war on France. 4 August: Germany invades Belgium; Britain declares war on Germany. Keep the early-July pledge, late-July ultimatum and August invasion separate; do not merge events under one date. Russia was mobilising before 1 August; do not date the beginning of its mobilisation to that day. France was allied with Russia; Germany was allied with Austria-Hungary, not Russia.

title: The outbreak of the First World War — Imperial War Museums
text: Nationalism, imperial competition, arms programmes and rival alliances shaped the crisis. The assassination provided a trigger, but leaders made decisions that escalated it. Germany backed Austria-Hungary; Austria-Hungary chose war against Serbia; Russia mobilised; German military planning targeted France through Belgium. Alliances did not automatically force every country to fight: Britain had no obligation to join under its agreements with France and Russia, and Italy initially stayed out because its alliance was defensive. British intervention reflected the invasion of Belgium and strategic concerns about Germany dominating Europe. Avoid describing war as inevitable or an automatic domino chain.
